page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance belonging to the ecs.se1ne family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance features 24 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, resulting in 24 vCPUs. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 architecture. Local storage is not bundled with this server, and network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is a bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also register poor to weak results. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks consistently place in the middle 50% of tested servers.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average multi-threaded performance, this instance is configured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-thread performance. Database operations, as indicated by average Passmark database scores and Redis SET operations of 16.8 million operations per second, represent a suitable fit. The instance also handles static web serving and software compilation at average performance levels. However, the lack of local storage and low baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps are key tradeoffs to consider when planning data-intensive or high-throughput network deployments.
